sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Yakubu Danladi, Luther Hon, Adedamola Aregbesola, Thelma Araokanmi, John Muniru & David Onoja. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Some Endangered West Chadic B.3 Languages in South Bauchi State, Nigeria with Notes on Dulubu [dbo]. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-019. Dallas: SIL International. 73 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 95036; downloaded via web.archive.org 20240907142714 snapshot of the sil.org PDF)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8.3 'Phonetic inventories' (pp. 26-27) gives a shared consonant chart and notes on prenasalization, labialization/palatalization, lateral fricatives; sec. 8.5.2 (pp. 30-32) Kir~Mansi segmental correspondences; Appendix F (p. 50) states 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' 222-item Kir wordlist (Kir Bangabut, 18 Aug 2020) carries impressionistic tone marks. Zero hits for stress/accent/syllable. Also reports Balar dialect extinct (p. 25).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Michael Bulkaam. 2021 [Glottolog 2020]. An introduction to Mantsi, a South Bauchi language of Central Nigeria. Draft, Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge. 25 pp. (sister language of Kir; held by the project)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes Mantsi (not Kir): three level tones plus rising/falling, no stress statement. Kir [Kyiir] appears only comparatively (Table 7 'Kir group innovations', ten Kir lexical items) and in a note that Cosper's unpublished ms. contained a Mantsi-Kir comparison omitted from Cosper 1999. Nothing on Kir prosody.

sources.note: 'kir' mentioned only as Shimizu's (1978) cluster 2 of South Bauchi; Caron's descriptive work covers South-Bauchi-West only. Nothing on Kir.
